short: The "Father of History", who wrote a sweeping narrative of the Greco-Persian Wars.
full:
Herodotus was a Greek historian who was born in Halicarnassus in the Persian Empire and later lived in Athens and Thurii. He is widely considered the first historian in the Western tradition, breaking from the Homeric tradition of mythological storytelling by engaging in systematic investigation. His single known work, The Histories, serves as a record of the ancient traditions, politics, geography, and clashes of various cultures that were known in Greece, Western Asia, and Northern Africa at that time.

The central narrative of The Histories focuses on the rise of the Persian Empire and the events of the Greco-Persian Wars. By interviewing witnesses and collecting disparate sources, Herodotus sought to explain the causes of the conflict between the Greek city-states and the massive empire to the east. Though later criticized for his occasional credulity and inclusion of fabulous tales, his methodology laid the foundations for the historical discipline and provided an invaluable record of the ancient Mediterranean world.
